- cross-phase conflicts can record the new vote but must also persist
  double-vote evidence,
- accepted PREPARE/COMMIT votes cache rosters and request commit-pipeline
  progress, while NEW_VIEW votes do not cache rosters; stale NEW_VIEW votes can
  aggregate a QC but must not update the proposal tracker or request the commit
  pipeline.

`SumeragiDropPrecommitVoteForLockGate.tla` captures
`drop_precommit_vote_for_lock(...)`:
- non-Commit votes and unlocked actors are allowed through the lock filter,
- Commit votes below the locked height are dropped with consensus handling but
  without vote-validation drop accounting,
- same-height conflicting Commit votes are dropped before payload lookup, even
  when the vote carries a newer view,
- same-hash votes and higher Commit votes are allowed while the locked payload
  or candidate payload remains unavailable,
- locally checkable higher same-view Commit votes must extend the locked chain,
  while newer-view higher votes use the shared locked-QC bypass.
Its TLC cross-check independently exhausts the same seventeen expected-failure
configs as Apalache.

`SumeragiEvidenceHorizonGate.tla` captures `evidence_within_horizon(...)`, the
stale-evidence admission helper:
- zero horizon disables the height gate and accepts any subject,
- missing evidence subject height defaults to the current committed height,
- positive horizons compare against `current_height.saturating_sub(horizon)`,
- the lower bound is inclusive, stale subjects below it are rejected, and
  future subjects remain accepted when they are above the lower bound.

`SumeragiEvidenceCanonicalizationGate.tla` captures evidence canonicalization
and deduplication helpers around `evidence_key(...)`, `canonicalize_evidence(...)`,
`evidence_subject_height_view(...)`, `evidence_block_refs(...)`,
`EvidenceStore::insert(...)`, and persistence record construction:
- double-vote and censorship evidence keys are order-insensitive, canonical,
  include the evidence kind and payload, and do not rewrite invalid QC/proposal
  payloads,
- subject height/view extraction follows each evidence kind, including
  committed-height defaults for missing subjects and zero-view defaults for
  censorship evidence,
- block references include valid QC and distinct double-vote block hashes while
  omitting proposal/censorship references and deduplicating same-hash root
  conflicts,
- store and persistence insertion validate before recording, reject duplicate
  and swapped-duplicate evidence, and store the canonical key without setting
  penalty side-effect flags.

`SumeragiEvidenceValidationGate.tla` captures `validate_evidence(...)`, the
fail-closed evidence validation helper:
- evidence kind/payload mismatches are rejected before payload-specific
  validation,
- double-vote validation enforces signature presence and length, supported
  phase pairs, matching height/epoch/topology-resolved signer, a real
  block-or-root conflict, evidence-kind agreement, and valid vote signatures,
- invalid-proposal validation requires the proposal height to advance beyond
  the referenced QC and its parent hash to match the QC subject, while proposal
  view numbers are intentionally not compared across heights,
- censorship validation requires non-empty receipts, matching transaction
  hashes, validator signers, valid receipt signatures, and an f + 1
  unique-signer quorum so duplicate receipts cannot inflate availability
  evidence.

`SumeragiDoubleVoteRecordingGate.tla` captures `check_double_vote(...)`,
`check_double_vote_with_context(...)`, and `record_double_vote(...)`:
- detection rejects mismatched height/epoch/signer, unsupported phase pairs,
  non-conflicting same-block votes, and out-of-range topology signers,
- topology-aware detection compares peers resolved for each vote view, so
  cross-view rotated indices for the same validator are accepted while equal raw
  indices resolving to different peers are rejected,
- PREPARE/COMMIT cross-phase equivocation and COMMIT root-only conflicts are
  recorded as `DoubleCommit` evidence with canonical order-insensitive keys,
- recording has no side effects when no evidence exists, stops before
  persistence when the in-memory store rejects an entry, calls persistence
  after store insertion, and returns false when persistence rejects a
  duplicate/stale entry while retaining the canonical in-memory key.

`SumeragiInvalidQcShapeGate.tla` captures
`check_invalid_commit_qc_shape(...)`, the intentionally narrow invalid-QC
shape-to-evidence helper:
- empty signer bitmaps always produce `InvalidQc` evidence,
- the zero sentinel requires both view and height to be zero; height zero alone
  and view zero alone do not emit evidence,
- emitted evidence keeps the `InvalidQc` kind, clones the supplied certificate,
  and uses the fixed diagnostic reason string,
- non-emitting valid certificates have no payload or reason side effects.

`SumeragiQcValidationEvidenceGate.tla` captures
`qc_validation_error_to_evidence(...)` and the evidence-returning part of
`validate_qc_with_evidence(...)`:
- hard QC validation failures emit `InvalidQc` evidence,
- soft missing-context or insufficient-quorum failures do not emit evidence,
- emitted evidence clones the failed QC and uses the error telemetry reason,
- successful validation returns `Ok` with no evidence.

`SumeragiQcValidationReasonGate.tla` captures
`QcValidationError::telemetry_reason()`, `qc_validation_reason(...)`, and the
reason projection used by `qc_validation_error_to_evidence(...)`:
- every QC validation error maps to its exact stable telemetry label,
- hard failures emit evidence whose reason matches the helper label,
- soft missing-context or insufficient-quorum failures keep their telemetry
  label but do not emit evidence,
- expected-failure mutations cover label drift and hard/soft evidence-boundary
  drift for every validation variant.

`SumeragiBlockSyncQcFallbackGate.tla` captures
`block_sync_qc_is_missing_context_error(...)` and
`block_sync_qc_aggregate_fallback_ok(...)`:
- block-sync retries only missing votes, unavailable stake snapshots, and
  aggregate mismatches that may resolve after sidecar/roster convergence,
- invalid signatures, out-of-bounds signers, and insufficient signers remain
  non-retryable validation failures,
- aggregate fallback accepts only COMMIT QCs without nested highest QC, with a
  valid aggregate and parseable bitmap,
- permissioned fallback requires the commit quorum with a one-signer floor, and
  NPoS fallback requires a stake snapshot, signer peers, and stake quorum.

`SumeragiBlockSyncQcStatusGate.tla` captures block-sync QC status accounting:
- invalid-signature batch drops, QC replacement, QC derivation failures,
  locked-QC prefilter drops, quarantine, and successful revalidation increment
  independent counters,
- final QC drops increment the final-drop counter and overwrite the last reason,
- repeated observations accumulate counters instead of overwriting them,
- `snapshot()` projects the counters and final-drop reason, and the block-sync
  test reset helper clears them.

`SumeragiBlockSyncLockedQcGate.tla` captures block-sync locked-QC helper gates:
- `block_sync_qc_extends_locked_chain(...)` allows no-lock QCs, allows
  missing-locked-payload QCs only when their view is newer than the lock, and
  otherwise delegates to locked-chain extension,
- `block_sync_qc_same_height_conflict(...)` requires same height, non-newer
  view, and hash conflict,
- `block_sync_qc_same_height_recoverable(...)` requires the explicit
  non-extending allowance flag, Commit phase, same height, and hash conflict,
- `defer_block_sync_qc_while_locked_payload_missing(...)` quarantines and
  records a dropped QC only for non-newer non-matching QCs while the locked
  payload is still locally unavailable,
- `block_sync_qc_is_stale_against_lock(...)` requires a lock, below-lock
  height, and non-newer view.

`SumeragiKnownBlockQcEnqueueGate.tla` captures
`enqueue_known_block_qc_work(...)`:
- `QcVoteKey` includes phase, subject block hash, height, view, epoch,
  chain-order hash, and rechain sequence,
- duplicate queued work is detected by that key and returns without inserting,
  overwriting, recording deferred status, or waking the loop,
- new work is inserted under the computed key and preserved for later drain,
- new work records `Qc` / `Deferred` / `AggregateVerifyDeferred` consensus
  status and emits queued-work debug metadata,
- wake signaling is attempted only when a wake sender is present,
- wake send failure is ignored after the work has been queued and accounted.

`SumeragiKnownBlockQcWorkGate.tla` captures
`prepare_known_block_qc_work(...)`:
- empty commit topologies invoke roster-unavailable recovery and return
  `None`,
- QC/block hash, height, epoch, and phase mismatches return `None` before
  locked-QC work is constructed,
- unrecoverable same-height locked-QC conflicts either delegate to missing
  locked-payload deferral or increment the locked-QC prefilter metric, log the
  conflict, record a dropped QC, and return `None`,
- stale QCs below the lock record a locked-QC drop and return `None`,
- non-extending known-block QCs are deferred only while the locked payload is
  missing; otherwise they are retained for lock realignment,
- successful work preserves the QC, block, topology, stake snapshot,
  consensus mode, mode tag, PRF seed, and commit-QC match flag, while setting
  `aggregate_ok = None`.

`SumeragiKnownBlockQcDrainGate.tla` captures
`drain_known_block_qc_work(...)`:
- empty known-block QC work queues return `false` without applying work,
- tick-budget exhaustion stops before removing or applying the next work item,
- at most `KNOWN_BLOCK_QC_WORK_PER_TICK` work items are removed and applied per
  drain call,
- remaining queued work is preserved when the per-tick cap or tick budget
  stops the drain,
- progress is returned only when at least one applied work item reports
  progress,
- processed-work debug logging is emitted only after at least one work item is
  drained.

`SumeragiSignedQuorumFetchFallbackGate.tla` captures
`committed_signed_quorum_fetch_fallback_available(...)` and
`signed_commit_quorum_signer_count(...)`:
- signer evidence is not consulted until the local committed hash at the block
  height matches the requested block,
- the exact round roster is used before the effective commit topology fallback,
- permissioned fallback requires valid block signers to meet
  `min_votes_for_commit().max(1)`,
- NPoS fallback requires a matching state/cache stake snapshot, signer peers
  mapped into the topology, and a successful stake quorum check.

`SumeragiCommitQcOnlyFetchResponseGate.tla` captures
`dispatch_commit_qc_only_fetch_response(...)`:
- direct commit-QC responses attempt an optional certified proof companion
  before sending the direct commit-QC companion,
- direct commit-QC responses skip cached-vote rebroadcast and signed-quorum
  fallback,
- when direct commit QC is unavailable, cached commit votes are rebroadcast to
  recovery targets plus the requester with deduplication,
- signed-quorum fallback sends a bypassed `BlockSyncUpdate` preserving the
  requester roster-proof flag and returns success,
- without direct commit QC and without signed-quorum fallback, the helper
  returns `false`.

`SumeragiBlockSyncUpdateTargetsGate.tla` captures
`block_sync_update_targets_for_peers(...)`:
- zero gossip limits and empty peer lists produce no targets,
- the local peer is never targeted,
- online registered or trusted strays are preferred before world peers, while
  unregistered strays are ignored,
- online world peers are used before offline world fallback candidates,
- the selected fanout never exceeds the configured gossip limit.

`SumeragiApplyCachedQcsGate.tla` captures
`apply_cached_qcs_to_block_sync_update(...)`:
- existing commit QCs and validator checkpoints on the update are preserved,
- topology-backed cache/history evidence is selected before raw cache evidence,
  signer-history derivation, and world fallback,
- a missing validator checkpoint is synthesized only when a final commit QC is
  attached,
- NPoS stake snapshots are repaired when absent or mismatched, while
  permissioned updates do not trigger stake repair,
- cached commit votes fill only an empty vote list and wrong-context votes are
  ignored.

`SumeragiBlockSyncRosterGate.tla` captures
`allow_uncertified_block_sync_roster(...)`:
- explicit missing-block requests allow the uncertified roster path for stale,
  same-height, next-height, and future-height block-sync payloads,
- unrequested block-sync payloads may use the uncertified roster path only for
  the exact next height,
- the next-height check mirrors Rust's saturating `u64` addition, so a local
  height already at the bounded maximum accepts the same maximum block height.

`SumeragiBlockSyncRosterStatusGate.tla` captures block-sync roster status
accounting:
- `commit_checkpoint_pair_hint` increments both commit-QC and checkpoint hint
  counters, while single-source labels increment only their own buckets,
- history, sidecar, and commit-roster-journal sources increment independent
  counters, and unknown source labels are no-ops,
- missing-proof and unsolicited-`ShareBlocks` drops increment their own
  counters,
- `snapshot().block_sync_roster` projects all roster source/drop counters and
  the test reset helper clears them.

`SumeragiBlockSyncWarningThrottleGate.tla` captures
`BlockSyncWarningThrottle::allow(...)` and `clear()`:
- warning keys include kind, block hash, height, and view, so independent
  conflict/missing-role contexts do not throttle each other,
- first warnings insert state and log immediately, while repeat warnings are
  suppressed only inside the strict cooldown window,
- warnings at the cooldown boundary replay the suppressed count, reset the
  counter, and refresh the last-emitted timestamp,
- burst caps apply globally within the burst window but a zero cap disables the
  burst limiter,
- GC uses `cooldown * 8` with a one-second floor for zero cooldown, retains
  exact-boundary entries, and prunes only expired entries,
- `clear()` resets both per-warning entries and burst-window accounting.

`SumeragiQcInsufficientWarningThrottleGate.tla` captures
`QcInsufficientWarningThrottle::allow(...)` and `clear()`:
- warning keys include kind, phase, block hash, height, and view, so
  permissioned-vote and NPoS-stake quorum warnings do not suppress each other
  or cross phases,
- first warnings insert state and log immediately, while repeat warnings are
  suppressed only inside the strict cooldown window,
- warnings at the cooldown boundary replay the suppressed count, reset the
  counter, and refresh the last-emitted timestamp,
- zero cooldown bypasses suppression, GC uses `cooldown * 8` with a one-second
  floor for zero cooldown, and `clear()` drops all tracked keys.

`SumeragiFetchResponseDeferralGate.tla` captures
`should_defer_canonical_committed_fetch_response(...)`:
- only the exact local committed height with a matching canonical committed
  hash can defer a fetch/body response,
- canonical `BlockCreated` payloads and canonical `BlockSyncUpdate` payloads
  without commit-QC or validator-checkpoint proof sidecars defer until proof is
  available,
- historical, future, hash-mismatched, hash-unknown, proof-bearing update, and
  non-payload message cases do not defer.

`SumeragiFetchBlockBodyHandleGate.tla` captures
`handle_fetch_block_body(...)`:
- exact local block-body requests dispatch only when the local block hash,
  height, and view match and canonical committed proof deferral is not needed,
- canonical committed deferrals stash the requester without dispatching or
  removing it,
- identity mismatches and absent local blocks fall through to the frontier-slot
  and pending-window stash policy instead of serving body material,
- a matching frontier slot wins over the broader pending-body window,
- every path releases its dedup key exactly once, and every non-dispatch path
  records a deferred/not-found outcome.

`SumeragiBackgroundFrameCapGate.tla` captures
`trim_block_sync_update_for_frame_cap(...)`,
`trim_block_body_response_for_frame_cap(...)`,
`direct_block_sync_update_fallback_for_body_response(...)`, and
`prepare_background_block_message(...)`:
- payload-carrying consensus messages use the payload frame cap while
  request/control messages use the ordinary consensus frame cap,
- oversized `BlockSyncUpdate` payloads trim commit votes first, then preserve
  the strongest fitting sidecar evidence for the consensus mode,
- permissioned updates may drop stale stake snapshots, while NPoS updates keep
  stake snapshots when splitting commit QC and validator checkpoint evidence,
- oversized `BlockBodyResponse(BlockSyncUpdate)` values trim the embedded
  update before downgrading and prefer a direct `BlockSyncUpdate` fallback when
  that direct proof-preserving update fits,
- messages that cannot be made to fit are dropped.

`SumeragiBackgroundDispatchGate.tla` captures
`background_request_allows_blocking(...)` and
`dispatch_background_request(...)`:
- every current `BackgroundRequest` variant is blocking-eligible, so a full
  background queue returns the reconstructed request for caller fallback,
- full queues record overflow but not drop status,
- missing or disconnected workers record drop status and still return the
  reconstructed request, and
- request kind labels and reconstructed request kinds stay stable across the
  telemetry and status accounting path.

`SumeragiBackgroundBypassGate.tla` captures the prepared-request branch table
in `schedule_background(...)` and `schedule_background_via_queue(...)`:
- normal scheduling bypasses the worker for proposal, proof, body-response,
  fetch-body, and RBC data/control payload posts named in the Rust branch,
- normal broadcast scheduling bypasses only the broadcast-safe proposal,
  body-response, and RBC payload kinds, while broadcast votes/QCs/fetch
  requests remain queued,
- control-flow and native-AMX requests remain queued in normal scheduling, and
- disabled-worker scheduling dispatches every accepted request inline, while
  `schedule_background_via_queue(...)` keeps even high-priority payloads queued.

`SumeragiBackgroundFallbackGate.tla` captures
`dispatch_background_fallback(...)`:
- post requests stay P2P posts and preserve their target peer, while broadcast
  requests stay P2P broadcasts without adding a peer target,
- consensus block, control-flow, and native-AMX requests preserve their network
  payload class, and
- block messages project their embedded consensus priority while control-flow
  and native-AMX messages are always high priority.

`SumeragiFetchPendingResponseSendGate.tla` captures
`send_fetch_pending_block_response(...)`:
- hintless `BlockSyncUpdate` responses are preserved only when hintless bypass
  is allowed and the requester already proved roster context; otherwise they
  are downgraded to `BlockCreated`,
- bypass decisions honor force, consensus priority, highest-QC targeting,
  eager body/RBC payload kinds, and accepted hintless responses,
- non-downgraded `BlockSyncUpdate` responses apply cached QCs before direct
  commit-QC extraction and frame-cap trimming,
- direct commit-QC companions are sent before the final payload, including
  fallback payloads, or before returning when the payload is dropped,
- unfit `BlockSyncUpdate` responses fall back to `BlockCreated` with the
  originally computed bypass decision, and drop payloads when that fallback is
  also oversized.

`SumeragiRequesterRosterProofGate.tla` captures
`requester_has_local_roster_proof(...)`:
- any one exact proof source is sufficient: committed roster snapshot,
  Commit-QC cache key, precommit signer record, or matching highest Commit QC,
- Commit-QC cache proof is keyed by phase, block hash, height, view, epoch,
  and vNext chain-order binding,
- precommit signer proof is keyed by block hash, height, view, and epoch, and
- highest-QC proof requires the Commit phase plus exact block hash, height,
  and view.

`SumeragiBlockSyncFutureWindowGate.tla` captures
`should_drop_future_block_sync_update(...)`:
- locally known blocks bypass all future-drop gates,
- requested missing-block recovery is allowed only inside the stale-height
  margin and is checked before parent availability,
- unresolved lower missing heights drop far-ahead unrequested updates before a
  known parent can short-circuit sparse chain admission,
- known parents admit connected unrequested updates before the generic future
  height/view window is consulted,
- the generic `BlockSyncUpdate` future window respects disabled windows,
  exclusive height/view boundaries, missing phase-view samples, and expired
  view-age grace.

`SumeragiBlockBodyRepairGate.tla` captures
`allow_rbc_session_block_body_repair(...)`:
- RBC block-body repair is allowed only when DA/RBC is enabled and the response
  height is exactly the local frontier slot,
- the response slot must have a matching RBC session whose metadata still
  matches local progress and which does not already hold an authoritative
  payload,
- both `BlockCreated` and `BlockSyncUpdate` bodies must carry the same block
  hash, height, view, and payload hash as the response/session.

`SumeragiBlockBodyRequestStashGate.tla` captures
`should_stash_pending_block_body_request(...)`:
- exact body requesters are retained only from the next committed slot through
  the configured missing-request stale-height margin,
- zero configured margin is floored to one so the frontier slot remains
  stashable,
- lower and upper window edges use saturating height arithmetic.

`SumeragiSameHeightBlockBodyRepairGate.tla` captures
`allow_same_height_block_body_repair(...)`:
- same-height body repair is rejected unless the response height is the exact
  local frontier slot,
- matching pending missing-block requests, matching deferred missing-payload
  commit QCs, and active missing commit-QC repair rounds are independent
  admission sources,
- pending requests and deferred QCs must match commit phase, block hash,
  height, view, and actionable-dependency checks.

`SumeragiBlockBodyRepairEpochGate.tla` captures
`observed_commit_qc_epoch_for_body_repair(...)`:
- exact cached commit-QC epochs have priority over every other source,
- matching deferred missing-payload commit QCs beat pending-block observed
  commit-QC epochs,
- deferred QCs must match commit phase, block hash, height, and view, while
  pending blocks must have an observed commit QC and a recorded epoch.

`SumeragiDirectCommitQcForBlockGate.tla` captures
`direct_commit_qc_for_block(...)`:
- cached commit QCs for the exact block are returned before consulting any
  other source,
- world-derived commit QCs are used before local vote formation,
- local vote formation uses the exact round roster when present, otherwise the
  effective commit topology,
- local vote formation only runs after the commit quorum floor is met, with a
  zero quorum floored to one vote.

`SumeragiMaterializeQcGate.tla` captures
`materialize_qc_for_header(...)` and the Kura recovery helper it uses:
- an existing cached QC for the requested header is returned immediately,
- empty rosters skip local vote formation and can only recover a commit QC from
  Kura plus precommit-signer history,
- non-empty rosters first try cached vote formation, then Kura recovery, then
  local signer aggregation,
- NPoS materialization requires a stake roster, signer mapping, and stake
  quorum, while permissioned materialization requires voting-signature quorum,
- commit-QC root filtering, empty signers, aggregate-signature errors, and
  incomplete canonical signer mapping all fail closed,
- recovered, formed, and rebuilt QCs are cached for later lookup.

`SumeragiEmbeddedQcRosterGate.tla` captures embedded-QC roster bootstrapping:
- embedded rosters must match the expected mode tag, be non-empty V1 rosters,
  carry the advertised validator-set hash, and avoid highest-QC payloads on
  non-NewView QCs,
- the embedded roster must match an authoritative topology candidate and every
  validator must have cached proof-of-possession material before validation,
- permissioned fallback requires voting quorum, while NPoS fallback requires a
  matching stake snapshot, valid signer mapping, and stake quorum,
- the caller replaces stale vote-roster cache entries and defers payload
  recovery only after certification plus QC validation or aggregate recovery.

Its TLC cross-check independently exhausts the same twenty-four
expected-failure configs as Apalache.

`SumeragiBlockBodyDirectCommitQcGate.tla` captures
`direct_commit_qc_from_block_body_response(...)`:
- body block hash, height, and view must match the response tuple before any
  commit QC can be detached,
- `BlockSyncUpdate` bodies prefer embedded commit QC, then validator-checkpoint
  derived QC, then local direct QC for the block,
- `BlockCreated` bodies can only detach a local direct QC for the block.

`SumeragiDetachedBlockBodyCommitQcGate.tla` captures
`handle_detached_block_body_commit_qc(...)`:
- absent detached QCs cause no handling or clear side effects,
- already cached target commit QCs clear obsolete missing-commit-QC repair
  without reprocessing the QC,
- otherwise `handle_qc` is attempted and the repair request is cleared only if
  the target commit QC is cached afterward, including when handling returned an
  error.

`SumeragiBlockBodyResponseDispatchGate.tla` captures
`dispatch_block_body_response_with_plain_fallback(...)`:
- a `BlockCreated` companion is sent only when its encoded frame fits,
- `BlockSyncUpdate` responses send a plain `BlockCreated` fallback before the
  rich BlockBodyResponse,
- the rich BlockBodyResponse is always sent, and any direct commit-QC companion
  is sent afterward,
- every dispatch uses the bypass/background path.

`SumeragiInvalidProposalEvidenceBuildGate.tla` captures
`invalid_proposal_evidence(...)` and `build_invalid_proposal_evidence(...)`:
- the wrapper always emits `InvalidProposal` evidence and preserves the
  proposal plus validation-error reason,
- the builder derives the proposer from the first block-signature index, or
  zero when the block has no signatures,
- the built proposal uses the block-header view, caller-supplied epoch and
  payload hash, and selected QC,
- the selected QC subject remains the proposal parent and its height stays
  below the built proposal height so downstream evidence validation accepts it.

`SumeragiProposalMismatchGate.tla` captures `detect_proposal_mismatch(...)`,
the proposal/header/payload consistency helper:
- mismatches are reported in implementation order: height, view, parent hash,
  transaction root, state root, then payload hash,
- missing block parent and transaction roots compare against the zero hash,
- a zero proposal state root is accepted as a compatibility value even when the
  block header carries an execution-result root,
- zero-state compatibility still allows a later payload-hash mismatch to be
  reported.

`SumeragiProposalCacheGate.tla` captures the bounded `ProposalCache` helper:
- hint and proposal maps enforce the configured limit independently,
- overflow evicts the lowest key from the overflowing map and increments the
  eviction count only for real evictions,
- `observed_at` is retained while either a hint or proposal remains for the
  key and is removed when the last entry for the key disappears,
- duplicate inserts replace rather than duplicate entries, and
  `prune_height_leq(...)` removes committed-height entries while preserving
  future entries.

`SumeragiProposalHintAdmissionGate.tla` captures inbound proposal-hint
admission:
- stale height/view hints, malformed highest-QC references, cached duplicates,
  committed-edge conflicts, local metadata mismatches, and locked-QC conflicts
  fail closed,
- missing future highest-QC dependencies are dropped as accepted metadata while
  exact block repair is requested; cross-view hints may be cached only as
  dependency context and same-view hints are not cached,
- accepted hints update PRF context, cache the hint, mark the slot observed,
  replay deferred votes, and prune old observed slots,
- highest-QC state changes only for newer references or same-slot Commit phase
  promotion; lock-lag catchup defers that update while preserving accepted hint
  side effects.

`SumeragiStaleProposalHintRepairGate.tla` captures the stale-view proposal hint
repair exception:
- stale hints bypass the stale-view drop only when DA is enabled, the hint
  targets the active height, and the local view is exactly one ahead,
- the hint highest QC must exactly match the latest committed QC by height,
  view, subject hash, and epoch,
- every denied stale hint remains a stale-view drop and does not cache hint
  metadata, mark the slot observed, or mutate highest-QC state.

`SumeragiStaleRbcHintRepairGate.tla` captures stale RBC repair through cached
proposal hints:
- stale RBC chunks without a session bypass the stale-view drop only when DA is
  enabled, the message kind may seed a session, and the height is the exact
  frontier,
- the cached proposal hint at the same height/view must name the same block
  hash,
- matching hinted chunks are stashed and arm exact frontier body repair, while
  every rejected stale RBC message still drops and has no chunk-stash or repair
  side effects.

`SumeragiProposalAdmissionGate.tla` captures inbound proposal metadata
admission:
- stale height/view proposals, mismatched proposal epochs, malformed highest-QC
  references, parent/highest-QC mismatches, committed-edge conflicts, local
  metadata mismatches, and locked-QC conflicts fail closed,
- missing future highest-QC dependencies arm exact repair and a defer marker
  without caching the proposal or marking the slot observed,
- accepted proposals update PRF context, sample leader context, mark the slot
  observed, cache the proposal, replay deferred votes, and prune old observed
  slots,
- proposal metadata alone must not wake the commit pipeline or record
  payload-phase progress.

`SumeragiBlockCreatedAdmissionGate.tla` captures direct `BlockCreated` payload
admission:
- local-removed, stale-height/view, lock-rejected sink, authoritative-owner
  conflict, empty-payload, hint-mismatch, locked-QC, proposal-preserve, and
  RBC-payload mismatch gates fail closed before pending payload mutation,
- duplicates refresh payload state without taking ownership, missing-highest
  hints preserve replay material while arming dependency repair, and
  pending-processing or commit-inflight slots preserve the body for replay,
- future-height payloads request parent or gap repair before admission
  continues,
- accepted payloads update pending state, mark the payload phase, clear
  relevant missing-block requests, and wake the commit pipeline; proposal
  context is cached only for accepted inline proposal material.
The fast configuration checks `BlockCreatedAdmissionExactness`, which groups
admission outcomes, state ownership, replay/repair, evidence/proposal context,
and commit-wakeup anchors.

`SumeragiEmptyBlockQcDropGate.tla` captures empty-block QC filtering:
- NewView QCs, unknown blocks, non-empty blocks, and empty blocks with due time
  triggers continue without empty-block cleanup,
- non-NewView QCs for locally known empty blocks without due triggers are
  dropped before downstream QC caching or lock/highest-QC mutation,
- the drop path records an invalid-payload QC outcome and clears matching
  pending, missing-request, RBC, QC cache/tally, proposal/hint, vote-log,
  vote-validation, roster-cache, and block-signer-cache state,
- `EmptyBlockQcDropExactness` composes drop/continue decisions,
  invalid-payload accounting, pending/request/RBC cleanup, QC cache/tally
  cleanup, proposal/hint cleanup, vote-log/validation cleanup, and
  roster/signer-cache cleanup.

`SumeragiBlockSyncRecoveryModeGate.tla` captures stale BlockCreated and
block-sync recovery-mode helper policy:
- heights at or below the committed height are stale, while higher heights
  remain fresh,
- stale `BlockCreated` recovery is admitted by any one of missing-request,
  retained-payload, or recovery-evidence signals and rejected without a signal,
- only signed-quorum and commit-evidence repair may supersede an authoritative
  frontier owner,
- only requested-payload and commit-evidence repair may bypass a missing stale
  recovery request,
- only commit-evidence repair with the explicit revival flag may revive an
  aborted pending block without a local commit QC, and only commit-evidence
  repair reports an observed commit-QC epoch.

`SumeragiMissingRequestClearGate.tla` captures missing-block request clear
helpers used by proposal and `BlockCreated` rejection paths:
- locked-QC rejections keep requests for the locked hash itself and for
  unresolved parentless branches whose conflict has not been locally proven,
- committed-history conflicts, durable locked-block competitors, and local
  ancestry conflicts against committed locks clear obsolete requests,
- stale `BlockCreated` drops clear requests below the committed tip, when the
  payload is locally available, or when committed history disproves the hash,
  while committed-height missing-payload repair requests stay live.

`SumeragiMissingBlockClearGate.tla` captures `missing_block_clear_allowed(...)`:
- payload-available clears require a locally known block payload before a
  missing-block request can be dropped,
- obsolete clears are allowed even when the block payload is not locally known,
- swapped reason handling, unconditional clears, and local-payload requirements
  for obsolete requests are expected-failure mutations.

`SumeragiProposalBudgetGate.tla` captures proposal-side budget/cap helpers:
- consensus queue backpressure floors zero block-payload and RBC chunk caps to
  one and trips at the exact cap boundary,
- DA payload budget is the minimum of block payload cap, RBC total chunk
  budget, and pending-RBC byte/chunk budget, with zero chunk sizes and pending
  chunk caps floored before multiplication,
- transaction budgets honor both block-parameter and runtime caps while still
  admitting at least one transaction for an empty queue,
- fast-finality transaction and gas caps apply when either raw or effective
  commit time is at the fast threshold, and missing base gas caps stay absent,
- proposal stale windows use ceiling batches, a full-batch grace multiplier,
  and the configured maximum multiplier cap.

`SumeragiProposalBackpressureGate.tla` captures proposal backpressure
classification helpers:
- `ProposalBackpressure::should_defer()` treats queue saturation, consensus
  worker-queue pressure, active pending blocks, RBC backlog, and relay
  pressure as immediate deferral signals,
- `ProposalBackpressure::only_pacing_backpressure()` is true only for queue
  saturation and/or consensus worker-queue pressure without active pending
  blocks, RBC backlog, or relay pressure,
- `proposal_backpressure_allows_queue_work(...)` admits queued proposal work
  when there is no deferral signal, or when the only deferral source is pacing
  backpressure.

`SumeragiProposalDeferWarningThrottleGate.tla` captures proposal-defer warning
throttle helpers:
- first observations for a `(kind, height, view, highest_hash)` key emit a
  warning and insert a zero-suppression entry,
- repeated observations within the cooldown keep the original timestamp,
  increment the suppressed count, and return no warning,
- cooldown-boundary and post-cooldown observations replay the suppressed count,
  reset it, and update the timestamp,
- empty-commit-topology proposal/finalize warnings normalize the view to zero
  while all other proposal-defer warning kinds remain view-specific,
- zero cooldown never suppresses, and GC retains entries through the inclusive
  expiry boundary while pruning older entries.

`SumeragiNonRbcPayloadBudgetGate.tla` captures non-RBC payload frame budgeting:
- the consensus payload frame cap is reduced by the fixed 8 KiB non-RBC
  headroom using saturating subtraction,
- an absent `block_max_payload_bytes` config uses the adjusted frame cap,
- an explicit config below or equal to the adjusted frame cap is preserved,
- an explicit config above the adjusted frame cap is clamped, including when
  the adjusted frame cap is zero.

`SumeragiProposalBatchGate.tla` captures proposal batch trimming and
canonicalization helpers:
- size-cap trimming removes only from the tail while excess bytes remain and
  never drops the final transaction,
- zero-sized transaction size entries are floored to one byte when reducing
  excess, so trimming cannot loop through extra entries,
- trimmed transactions are recorded in pop order with their routing decision or
  routing plan still aligned,
- canonicalization sorts by transaction key and original index, preserving
  stable order for duplicate keys,
- transaction, routing, routing-plan, and size vectors are reordered together
  without changing batch length or mutating empty/singleton batches.

`SumeragiLaneInterleaveGate.tla` captures lane interleaving for routing
decisions:
- empty and singleton inputs preserve index order without fabricating or
  dropping indices,
- single-lane inputs remain in original order even when the slot would rotate a
  multi-lane start offset,
- multi-lane inputs round-robin by sorted lane id while preserving original
  order within each lane,
- height/view-derived offsets rotate the starting lane and wrap modulo the
  number of lanes.

`SumeragiCommitmentSnapshotBuilderGate.tla` captures
`build_commitment_snapshots_from_totals(...)`:
- lane commitment snapshots copy the committed block height/hash, lane id, tx
  count, total chunks, RBC byte total, and TEU total from each sorted lane
  aggregate entry,
- dataspace commitment snapshots also preserve the dataspace id from each
  sorted `(lane_id, dataspace_id)` aggregate key,
- lane and dataspace outputs follow BTreeMap order so status consumers see
  deterministic snapshot vectors.

`SumeragiCollectorPlanGate.tla` captures the bounded `CollectorPlan` helper:
- new and default plans preserve the target list and start with zero sent
  collectors,
- restored plans cap the supplied sent count at the target length so retry
  state cannot point beyond the plan,
- `peek()` reports the current target without advancing the sent count,
- `next()` reports the current target and advances by one, while exhausted
  plans return no target and keep their sent count,
- the gossip fallback trigger returns `true` exactly once and keeps the
  triggered flag set afterwards.
- `CollectorPlanRetryGossipExactness` composes constructor preservation,
  restored sent-count capping, read-only peek, exact next advancement,
  exhaustion semantics, and one-shot gossip fallback into one aggregate
  invariant.

`SumeragiCollectorSelectionGate.tla` captures the topology collector-selection
helpers feeding `CollectorPlan`:
- commit quorum and proxy-tail indices follow `commit_quorum_from_len(...)`
  and `proxy_tail_index()`,
- the effective collector fanout is zero for empty/zero-k inputs, one for
  positive single-peer inputs, and otherwise quorum-floored but capped to the
  non-leader set,
- default collector indices form the non-wrapping slice starting at the proxy
  tail, while fallback indices wrap from the proxy tail to fill the effective
  fanout without selecting the leader,
- PRF-backed selection is abstracted to distinct, in-range non-leader
  collectors, and `deterministic_collectors(...)` chooses PRF output exactly
  when a seed is present.
- `CollectorSelectionExactness` composes exact quorum/proxy-tail derivation,
  effective fanout, default and fallback collector selection, PRF selection, and
  deterministic seed-based source routing across every bounded case.

`SumeragiTopologyMutationGate.tla` captures ordered-roster mutation helpers:
- `Topology::new(...)` deduplicates peers while preserving first-seen order,
- `rotate_preserve_view_to_front(...)` rotates by `idx % len`, leaves empty
  rosters unchanged, and preserves the current view-change index,
- `nth_rotation(...)` rejects view rewinds, returns the exact rotation delta,
  rotates only by `delta % len`, and records the target view-change index,
- `update_peer_list(...)` keeps retained existing peers in current topology
  order, appends first-seen new peers from the incoming list, and preserves the
  view-change index,
- `block_committed(...)` applies the same membership update and resets the
  view-change index to zero,
- `canonicalize_order(...)` sorts and deduplicates without resetting the
  view-change index.
- `TopologyOrderedRosterMutationExactness` composes exact rotate, forward-only
  `nth_rotation`, deduplicating construction, peer-list update, block-commit
  reset, and canonicalization behavior across every bounded case.

`SumeragiPrfLeaderShuffleGate.tla` captures PRF topology permutation helpers:
- `leader_index_prf(...)` returns zero for empty rosters and otherwise selects
  from the seed/height permutation by `view % len`,
- one full view cycle over a fixed seed/height visits each validator exactly
  once and repeats only after the roster length,
- `shuffle_prf(...)` leaves empty and single-peer rosters unchanged while
  applying a deterministic permutation for multi-peer rosters, and
- `shuffled_for_prf_seed(...)` canonicalizes and deduplicates peers before
  shuffling, then returns a view-zero topology.
- `PrfLeaderShuffleExactness` composes exact leader selection, cycle
  periodicity/distinctness, shuffle permutation behavior, and wrapper
  canonicalization/deduplication plus view reset across every bounded case.

`SumeragiTopologyFanoutGate.tla` captures topology fanout and redundant-send
helpers used by retry/rebroadcast paths:
- `redundant_send_r_from_len(...)` follows `2f + 1` with
  `f = floor((n - 1) / 3)`, treats zero length as one, and clamps at `u8::MAX`,
- `min_votes_for_view_change()` follows `f + 1` and never exceeds the active
  roster size for non-empty topologies,
- `redundant_send_r_floor(...)` raises configured fanout to the commit quorum,
  preserves larger configured values, floors zero to one, and clamps quorum
  conversion at `u8::MAX`,
- `topology_fanout_from_tail(...)` returns no targets for single-peer or
  zero-count inputs, otherwise starts at the proxy tail, wraps once as needed,
  skips the leader, preserves uniqueness, and caps to the non-leader set.
- `TopologyFanoutHelperExactness` composes redundant-send count, view-change
  quorum, configured redundant floor, and tail fanout selection exactness across
  every bounded case.

`SumeragiTopologyRoleFilterGate.tla` captures topology role classification and
role-filtered signature selection:
- `Topology::role(...)` partitions peers into leader, Set A validator, proxy
  tail, Set B validator, or undefined using the commit-quorum proxy-tail index,
- `NonEmptyTopology::leader(...)` and
  `ConsensusTopology::{leader, proxy_tail, validating_peers,
  set_b_validators, voting_peers}` expose the same slices as the role
  partition,
- `filter_signatures_by_roles(...)` rejects invalid signature indices, keeps
  only requested roles, preserves input signature order, preserves duplicate
  signatures, and keeps the single-peer proxy-tail filtering special case,
- `audit_roles_for_prev_block_hash(...)` canonicalizes, deduplicates, rotates
  the commit-quorum prefix from the previous block hash, then labels roles in
  the rotated topology order.
- `TopologyRoleFilterExactness` composes exact role partitioning, role-slice
  projection, role-filtered signature preservation, and audit-role
  canonicalization/rotation across every bounded case.

`SumeragiActiveTopologySelectionGate.tla` captures active validator topology
selection in `derive_active_topology_from_views(...)`:
- commit topology is preferred over world peers, and world peers are preferred
  over trusted-peer fallback when the earlier source is non-empty,
- every emitted roster is BLS-filtered, deduplicated, and canonicalized before
  it can drive signer indices,
- incomplete PoP maps do not filter commit/world-derived primary rosters, but
  trusted-derived rosters drop peers missing PoPs,
- complete PoP filters must either preserve quorum or fall back to the

- `ActiveTopologySelectionExactness` composes exact source-priority,
  BLS/dedup/canonical output normalization, PoP filtering/quorum-guard, and
  final trusted-fallback behavior across every bounded case.

`SumeragiP2pTopologyTrustedGate.tla` captures trusted-peer P2P topology refresh
helpers:
- `p2p_topology_with_trusted(...)` includes every world peer, the local trusted
  peer, and configured trusted peers in one deduplicated expected topology,
- configured trusted observers are not classified as stray online peers,
- `peer_ids_outside_topology(...)` returns only online peers outside the
  expected topology while preserving observed order and duplicate stray

- `TrustedP2pTopologyExactness` composes exact trusted-topology union/dedup
  behavior with outside-peer filtering, trusted-observer non-stray handling, and

`SumeragiP2pTopologyRefreshGate.tla` captures P2P topology refresh
coordination:
- `topology_refresh_decision(...)` skips empty world peer sets, suppresses
  unchanged clean refreshes, advertises changed world topology, and uses a
  stray-peer rebroadcast when online peers fall outside the expected topology,
- `topology_advertisement_for_refresh(...)` only returns an advertised peer set
  for changed or stray refreshes, and that set is the current world topology,
- `refresh_p2p_topology_with_current(...)` latches the local peer after it is
  seen in world state, sets the local-removed flag only after a later non-empty

  local removal instead of running the normal network update,
- normal refreshes clear the local-removed status, update `last_advertised` to
  the current world set, gossip only the world set, and update the network with

- `P2pTopologyRefreshExactness` composes exact decision/last-state updates,
  gossip and network advertisement behavior, local-seen/removal handling,
  queue clearing, idle skips, and stray-count propagation.

`SumeragiQuorumRetransmitTargetsGate.tla` captures
`quorum_retransmit_targets_for_missing_votes(...)`, the commit-vote repair
target selector:
- empty topologies and single-local topologies produce no remote targets,
- below commit quorum, retransmit targets are exactly the canonical non-local
  peers not already mapped from observed commit-vote signers,
- when one more vote would satisfy commit quorum, target selection expands to
  every non-local peer so partial vote sets can merge,
- a zero commit threshold does not trigger near-quorum full fanout, and an
  already-satisfied quorum falls back to missing-peer targeting,
- signer-mapping failure conservatively targets every non-local peer,
- targets preserve canonical topology order, exclude the local peer, and remain
  distinct.
- `QuorumRetransmitTargetExactness` composes exact empty/local-only no-op
  behavior, missing-voter targeting, near-quorum full fanout, mapping-failure
  fallback, local exclusion, canonical ordering, duplicate rejection, and
  view-mapped signer resolution.

`SumeragiRetransmitBackpressureGate.tla` captures retransmit pacing helpers in
`main_loop/reschedule.rs`:
- transaction queue pressure contributes 0/1/2/3 points at capacity-zero,
  60%, 80%, 95%, and saturation boundaries,
- RBC pressure level and RBC store bytes add to the queue score instead of
  replacing it,
- target throttling preserves a deterministic liveness floor under heavy
  pressure and returns zero only when there are no known targets,
- cooldown multipliers step at pressure scores 2, 4, and 6,
- consensus-ingress and near-quorum backlog expand reschedule backoff while
  zero base backoff remains zero,
- near-quorum payload repair timeout is `2 * rebroadcast_cooldown` clamped to
  the 200ms..2000ms window.
- `RetransmitBackpressurePacingExactness` composes exact queue pressure
  thresholds, RBC level/byte pressure, additive scoring, target-limit liveness
  floors, cooldown multipliers, backlog backoff precedence, and timeout clamps.

`SumeragiPacedRetransmitTargetsGate.tla` captures deterministic target
selection in `paced_retransmit_targets(...)` after the pressure helper chooses
a limit:
- zero limits and empty target lists return no targets,
- target lists already within the limit preserve their original order and
  duplicates because the helper returns before sorting,
- over-limit target lists are sorted and deduplicated before a second
  fits-within-limit check,
- still-over-limit lists rotate left by the height/view-derived offset modulo
  the deduplicated length, and
- the rotated list is truncated exactly to the requested limit.
- `PacedRetransmitTargetSelectionExactness` composes exact fail-closed
  zero/empty handling, pre-cap order and duplicate preservation, sort/dedup
  behavior, deterministic height/view offset rotation, and exact limit
  truncation.

`SumeragiQuorumRescheduleBackoffGate.tla` captures quorum-reschedule backoff
and contiguous-frontier fast resend helpers:
- zero base backoff returns zero and never escalates,
- vote deficit selects the 3x/2x/1x base multiplier before stall escalation,
- zero quorum timeout disables stall-age escalation regardless of stall age,
- moderate and severe stall boundaries raise the multiplier to at least 4x
  and 5x respectively and report escalation,
- resend windows clamp zero rebroadcast cooldown to 1ms,
- contiguous-frontier fast resend is enabled only for contiguous, vote-backed,
  below-quorum pending blocks with no relay, vote-queue, or RBC-availability
  backpressure.
- `QuorumRescheduleBackoffExactness` composes exact zero-base handling,
  deficit multiplier arithmetic, stall escalation boundaries, resend-window
  clamping, accepted fast-resend windows, and every fast-resend rejection gate.

`SumeragiRbcAvailabilityRescheduleGate.tla` captures
`rbc_availability_unresolved_for_reschedule(...)`:
- DA-disabled, timed-out, local-payload, absent, invalid, delivered,
  complete-ready, and zero-total READY sessions fail open,
- pending entries, zero-timeout pending entries, missing chunks, missing READY
  quorum, and complete-but-not-ready sessions block rescheduling before
  timeout, and
- `RbcAvailabilityRescheduleExactness` composes exact fail-open gates,
  terminal-session exits, pending-entry blocks, missing-chunk blocks, and
  missing-READY quorum blocks.

`SumeragiVoteBackedReassemblyStallGate.tla` captures the vote-backed
same-height frontier reassembly stall helpers:
- hard-cap arithmetic uses `2 * max(frontier_recovery_window,
  quorum_timeout, resend_window, 1ms)`,
- same-height frontier slots are owner sources only when the exact height,
  height, view, active mode, and `quorum_timeout` reason all match,
- rejected slots fall through to matching `frontier_recovery` state rather
  than blocking recovery-state ownership,
- owner stall age uses the latest slot/recovery progress timestamp, and
- expiry requires both owner stall age and quorum stall age to reach the hard
  cap.
- `VoteBackedReassemblyStallExactness` composes exact hard-cap arithmetic,
  accepted/rejected slot ownership, recovery ownership and fallback,
  latest-progress age selection, and expiry thresholds.

`SumeragiCompletedQuorumViewAdvanceGate.tla` captures the deterministic view
advance after completed quorum reschedule work:
- exact contiguous-frontier heights route through
  `OnViewAdvanceRequested` and then the exhausted-frontier view-change path,
  avoiding the generic repair suppression gate,
- missing or stale exact-frontier slots fall back to the committed frontier
  height and requested view instead of using stale slot state,
- non-exact lower/future heights route through
  `trigger_view_change_with_cause(...)` with the original height/view/cause,
- exact slot events choose `max(active_view, requested_view, candidate_view)`,
  advance by one with saturation, update progress timestamps, and
- exact slot events clear the quorum-timeout rebroadcast latch while generic
  routing preserves slot state.
- `CompletedQuorumViewAdvanceExactness` composes exact slot routing, exact
  no-slot/stale-slot fallback, generic routing, current-view max selection,
  slot-state mutation, cause preservation, and generic slot-state preservation.

`SumeragiQuorumRebroadcastDispatchGate.tla` captures pending-block rebroadcast
dispatch after quorum-reschedule target selection and pacing have already run:
- local vote emission requires a non-dropped pending block and non-empty
  topology,
- relay backpressure, empty targets, cooldown, zero backlog limits, and empty
  paced targets remain fail-closed,
- forced vote-backed repair fanout bypasses cooldown and target-limit
  throttles while still replaying votes,
- missing commit-QC fetches and `BlockCreated` replay require non-dropped
  vote-backed pending state, and
- contiguous near-quorum frontier blocks may send a fitting non-local
  `BlockSyncUpdate` while any actual work stamps the rebroadcast marker.
- `QuorumRebroadcastDispatchExactness` composes local-vote gating,
  fail-closed exits, forced fanout, vote replay, payload dispatch, block-sync
  dispatch, and rebroadcast marker stamping.

`SumeragiIsolatedVoteBackedHandoffGate.tla` captures the isolated one-vote
frontier handoff path in
`maybe_handoff_isolated_vote_backed_frontier_to_anchor(...)`:
- admission requires resilience to be enabled, exactly one observed vote, the
  vote count to remain below quorum, next-height contiguity, and no cached
  commit QC,
- admitted attempts seed quorum-timeout frontier recovery and feed the
  available body through the body-availability event path before slot
  validation,
- the resulting slot must still match the requested height/view/hash, carry a
  body, have no commit QC, and remain vote-backed by its owner state, and
- successful handoff returns true only when the anchor range-pull request is
  sent with the `frontier_stall_reset_fallback` reason.
- `IsolatedVoteBackedHandoffExactness` composes admission rejection, admitted
  recovery/body-event side effects, slot validation, anchor requests, range-pull
  action results, and reason labeling.

`SumeragiPreemptiveVoteBackedRetransmitGate.tla` captures the pre-timeout
vote-backed frontier retransmit handoff around
`preemptive_rebroadcast_vote_backed_frontier_block(...)`:
- candidates require an available resend window, observed votes, no QC,
  no validation or missing-local-data blocker, same-height recovery permission,
  stall age inside the resend/quorum-timeout window, and a due precommit
  rebroadcast window,
- missing pending blocks produce no action and do not synthesize pending state,
- non-empty vote rosters are preferred, empty vote rosters fall back to the
  effective commit topology, and empty combined targets fail closed while
  preserving the pending block,
- progress is reported only when downstream rebroadcast emits votes,
  `BlockSyncUpdate`, or `BlockCreated`, and
- the downstream near-quorum flag is exactly `vote_count < min_votes_for_commit`
  for both below-quorum and at-quorum retransmit candidates.
- `PreemptiveVoteBackedRetransmitExactness` composes candidate rejection and
  admission, missing-pending preservation, target-source selection, output-based
  progress, pending retention, and near-quorum flag exactness.

`SumeragiNearQuorumPreemptiveEscalationGate.tla` captures the pre-timeout
near-quorum missing-payload recovery escalation loop in
`reschedule_stale_pending_blocks(...)`:
- each tick processes at most one near-quorum recovery candidate, so a second
  candidate cannot bypass the per-tick cap,
- an exhausted tick budget marks `budget_exhausted` and suppresses escalation,
  and missing pending blocks also fail closed,
- fresh matching missing-block requests suppress duplicate fetches only when
  their height/view match, their dependency is actionable, and their age is
  below `min(max(retry_window, 1ms), max(2 * rebroadcast_cooldown, 1ms))`,
- fresh in-flight recovery range pulls suppress duplicates only when the
  stored hash/view match, the range pull is in flight, and its age is below
  `max(recovery_missing_block_height_ttl, 1ms)`, and
- escalation counts and progress are recorded only when
  `maybe_escalate_missing_block_height_recovery(...)` returns true.
- `NearQuorumPreemptiveEscalationExactness` composes budget and missing-pending
  fail-closed gates, fresh-request suppression, in-flight suppression, delegate
  result authority, per-tick cap enforcement, and progress/counter consistency.

`SumeragiManifestGateRescheduleGate.tla` captures the `ManifestGuard` branch
inside `reschedule_pending_quorum_block(...)`:
- pending blocks stopped at the DA manifest guard count as effective
  reschedule work so zero-vote manifest stalls are not dropped as zombie state,
- manifest-gated pending blocks are retained and marked as plain
  quorum-reschedule attempts only after the normal action path is admitted,
- manifest-gated blocks do not trigger immediate authoritative frontier
  rotation, even when the local payload is already available,
- empty retransmit-target sets remain no-op reschedules and do not stamp a
  fresh quorum-reschedule marker.
- `ManifestGateRescheduleExactness` composes manifest effectiveness,
  manifest-action and manifest-no-target behavior, plain zero-work cleanup,
  vote-backed action and no-target behavior, authoritative rotation
  admission/suppression, and passive vote-backed evidence preservation.

`SumeragiQcSignerBitmap.tla` captures QC signer-bitmap admission:
- bitmap length must match the topology-derived byte length,
- signer bits outside the topology are rejected,
- only signer indices inside the voting validator set count toward quorum,
- observer or padding indices cannot satisfy quorum on behalf of voting
  validators,
- accepted QC signer evidence must match the voting-set quorum predicate.
- `QcSignerBitmapAdmissionExactness` composes topology-width matching,
  parser/spec equality, voting-only quorum accounting, observer/padding
  rejection, out-of-bounds rejection, length-mismatch rejection, and accepted
  evidence exactness.

`SumeragiQcSignerCountGate.tla` captures the raw `qc_signer_count(...)`
projection:
- empty bitmaps and zero bytes count as zero signers,
- the low and high bits of each byte contribute equally through byte
  population count,
- multi-byte bitmaps sum every byte without truncation or saturation, and
- malformed padding bits are still counted because the helper has no roster
  context and reports the raw aggregate bitmap population.
- `QcSignerRawCountExactness` composes bitmap-width bounds, raw anchor counts,
  empty/zero-byte handling, single-bit handling, full-byte and padding-bit
  handling, and multi-byte accumulation.

`SumeragiBuildSignersBitmapGate.tla` captures QC signer-bitmap construction:
- zero-length rosters return an empty bitmap,
- non-empty rosters allocate exactly `ceil(roster_len / 8)` bytes, including
  partially filled final bytes,
- signer indexes map to little-endian bits inside each byte, including the
  `7 -> byte 0 bit 7` and `8 -> byte 1 bit 0` boundary,
- multiple in-range signers are ORed into the bitmap and full-roster bitmaps
  preserve every valid signer,
- duplicate observations collapse through the `BTreeSet` input, and
  out-of-roster/padding indexes never set bits or extend the bitmap.
- `BuildSignersBitmapExactness` composes exact bitmap length, zero-roster and
  non-empty allocation behavior, single-signer bit placement, multi-signer OR
  behavior, out-of-range/padding filtering, duplicate collapse, and full-roster
  coverage.

`SumeragiSignerIndexNormalizationGate.tla` captures canonical/view signer-index
normalization:
- view-specific signer indexes map back to canonical indexes by peer identity,
  not by numeric position,
- canonical signer indexes map into PRF-shuffled view topologies by peer
  identity and return `None` when the canonical roster is empty, the canonical
  index is invalid, or the peer is absent from the view topology,
- normalization filters out-of-range and absent peers instead of fabricating
  signer indexes,
- repeated peer observations collapse through set semantics, and
- canonical signers whose peers are present in both topologies round-trip
  through view indexes without changing the canonical set.
- `SignerIndexNormalizationExactness` composes canonical normalization anchors,
  canonical-to-view index lookup, canonical-set-to-view normalization,
  round-trip preservation/filtering, and exact actual/spec result equality.

`SumeragiCommitRootConsistency.tla` captures commit-QC execution-root
consistency:
- commit votes are filtered into one same-root group before quorum is
  evaluated,
- permissioned mode selects the largest same-root signer group with a
  deterministic low-root tie-break,
- NPoS mode selects the heaviest same-root stake group with the same tie-break,
- wrong-context votes cannot help satisfy quorum,
- QC validation rejects signer votes whose roots do not match the QC roots.
- `CommitRootConsistencyExactness` composes root selection/evidence exactness,
  permissioned and NPoS quorum exactness, mixed-root rejection, wrong-context
  signer/stake rejection, and QC root-validation exactness.

`SumeragiCommitPipelineRecoveryGate.tla` captures adapter-side commit-pipeline
recovery ordering:
- cached commit-vote quorums must be aggregated into a local commit QC before
  peer missing-QC recovery is armed,
- the locally formed commit-QC marker must stay attached to the pending block,
- missing commit-QC recovery is armed only for a valid, payload-local, stale,
  locally voted pending block that still extends the committed tip,
- fresh local votes, existing commit QCs, missing local DA payloads, invalid
  pending blocks, missing local votes, and off-tip candidates do not arm peer
  recovery,
- cached near-quorum commit votes are rebroadcast to quorum missing-signer
  targets, not the proposal collector subset, and empty/committed vote sets do
  not rebroadcast.
- `CommitPipelineRecoveryExactness` composes local commit-QC ordering,
  missing-QC recovery gates, and quorum retransmit target exactness.

`SumeragiKnownBlockCommitQcRecoveryGate.tla` captures known-block commit-QC
recovery helpers:
- a locally materialized payload requests commit-QC-only recovery while a
  missing local payload requests the block body,
- pending candidates must extend the current committed tip by exactly one
  height with a matching parent hash,
- stale-view commit-QC fetches are admitted only for the next committed height
  when either the explicit pending override or the pending map entry matches
  hash, height, view, validation state, consensus activity, local commit-vote
  emission, and tip-extension requirements,
- a bad explicit override does not block a valid map entry, and a valid
  explicit override does not require a valid map entry.
- `KnownBlockCommitQcRecoveryExactness` composes recovery request planning,
  pending tip-extension, and stale-view commit-QC fetch admission exactness.

`SumeragiStaleViewCommitQcFetchGate.tla` captures stale-view commit-QC fetch
admission:
- the requested block hash, height, and view must match the pending block
  exactly,
- invalid pending blocks, consensus-inactive pending blocks, and pending blocks
  without a local commit vote cannot authorize a fetch,
- tip extension requires the pending block to be exactly one height beyond the
  current tip with matching parent/tip hashes, and
- the all-absent parent/tip genesis case remains valid.
- `StaleViewCommitQcFetchExactness` composes exact request identity,
  pending-state/local-vote gates, tip-extension behavior, and positive
  admission exactness.

`SumeragiCommitAnchorQcGate.tla` captures commit-anchor QC promotion:
- `highest_qc` keeps an existing strictly newer `(height, view)` pair and
  otherwise adopts the incoming commit anchor,
- `locked_qc` keeps an existing equal-or-newer pair and otherwise adopts the
  incoming commit anchor,
- precommit votes are pruned exactly when the lock changes,
- a retained highest QC that no longer satisfies the locked chain is realigned
  back to the lock,
- highest/locked QC status publication reflects the final selections after any
  realignment.
- `CommitAnchorQcPromotionExactness` composes highest and locked QC selection,
  precommit pruning, realignment, and status publication exactness.

`SumeragiCommittedHeightQcGate.tla` captures committed-height QC admission:
- future-height QCs continue through normal QC processing,
- already committed matching-hash QCs are recorded only, with commit-QC roster
  and missing-request cleanup side effects kept commit-phase-only,
- matching NewView QCs replay deferred votes and payload repair requests,
- unknown committed-height blocks drop with the `Committed` reason,
- divergent committed-height hashes drop as commit conflicts, and divergent
  Commit QCs validate the incoming hash/height/view/epoch/mode/chain/stake
  context before valid conflicts emit `InvalidQc` evidence with the
  `commit_conflict_finality` reason.
- `CommittedHeightQcAdmissionExactness` composes admission decisions, drop
  reasons, record-only side effects, divergent-commit validation context, and
  finality-conflict evidence exactness.

`SumeragiPendingProgressGate.tla` captures pending-progress accounting helpers:
- progress touches update only exact, non-aborted pending-map or commit-inflight
  owners whose hash, height, and view match the event,
- activation refreshes reset inserted/progress timestamps and clear quorum
  reschedule and validation-redrive timers for exact, non-aborted owners,
- post-commit activation refreshes only pending-map entries that extend the new
  committed tip by exactly one height with the matching parent hash,
- RBC recent-progress gating is disabled for a zero window and otherwise
  accepts non-aborted pending-map or commit-inflight owners in the inclusive
  `[tip-1, tip+2]` height window whose progress age is within the window,
- `PendingProgressAccountingExactness` composes touch output, activation-window
  refresh output, tip-activation refresh output, and recent-progress window
  output exactness.

`SumeragiPendingBlockLifecycleGate.tla` captures `PendingBlock` lifecycle
helpers:
- new pending blocks start active, non-retired, validation-pending, awaiting the
  local commit vote, and free of DA-gate, retry, scheduler, root/artifact, and
  commit-evidence replay state,
- same-subject replacements replace the block/payload source while preserving
  lifecycle state,
- different-subject replacements reset validation, commit stage, DA gates, Kura
  retry state, scheduler state, execution roots, validated artifacts, and
  commit-evidence replay state,
- abort, retire, revive, and retired-payload refresh paths set the
  active/retired accessors and reset or preserve commit stage, Kura persistence,
  scheduler, and artifact state according to the concrete helper contracts,
- `PendingBlockLifecycleExactness` composes constructor defaults, same-subject
  replacement, different-subject replacement, revive, retire/abort, and
  retired-payload refresh exactness.

`SumeragiPendingBlockMarkerGate.tla` captures `PendingBlock` progress markers
and cooldown gates:
- local commit-vote emission advances only awaiting blocks, makes the
  local-vote accessor true, and touches progress exactly once,
- commit-QC observation dominates local-vote state, records the observed epoch,
  and touches progress only for first observation or epoch changes,
- reset returns the commit stage to awaiting and clears the commit-QC epoch,
- quorum reschedule, precommit rebroadcast, and validation redrive cooldowns
  treat missing prior attempts as due, use inclusive deadline boundaries, and
  rely on saturating elapsed time,
- vote-backed quorum reschedules additionally require stale pending progress
  and a strictly higher vote count after a previous vote-backed attempt,
- `PendingBlockMarkerCooldownExactness` composes commit-stage marker,
  quorum-reschedule cooldown, vote-backed reschedule, reschedule marker,
  precommit rebroadcast, and validation-redrive exactness.

`SumeragiKuraRetryGate.tla` captures `PendingBlock` Kura persistence retry
helpers:
- `kura_retry_due(...)` treats missing retry deadlines as due, uses inclusive
  deadline boundaries, and suppresses retries after abort,
- `reset_kura_retry(...)` clears attempts, retry deadline, and abort state,
- `mark_kura_persisted(...)` records durability and applies the same retry
  reset,
- `note_kura_failure(...)` increments attempts before scheduling exponential
  backoff, aborts without incrementing when the configured retry budget is
  zero, aborts after max-attempt exhaustion, and aborts with a cleared deadline
  when checked-add overflow prevents scheduling, and
- public retry delay reporting clamps oversized millisecond values to the u32
  surface while preserving the scheduled retry state,
- `KuraRetryStateExactness` composes due-state, reset/persisted reset,
  max-attempt, backoff, abort-boundary, and delay-reporting exactness.

`SumeragiCommitPipelineSchedulingGate.tla` captures commit-pipeline scheduling
before recovery/finalization candidates are processed:
- ticks enter the commit pipeline only when active candidates, commit inflight
  work, or an explicit commit wakeup exists; queue saturation alone does not
  run the pipeline,
- event-triggered entry is unconditional unless the local budget is already
  exhausted, and backlog observation cannot suppress or invent candidate work,
- recovery candidates are included only for explicit commit wakeups, queue
  saturation, or active candidates with commit-certificate evidence,
- the shared tick budget is bypassed only for active pending work under commit
  wakeup or queue saturation, and budget exhaustion re-arms the commit wakeup
  without processing candidates,
- idle-view repair preserves its budget only when a woken commit pipeline has
  active pending candidates.
- `CommitPipelineSchedulingExactness` composes pipeline entry, recovery-scope,
  deadline/budget, wakeup/event, candidate-progress, and idle-budget exactness.

`SumeragiPrecommitVoteCountGate.tla` captures precommit vote counting:
- only COMMIT-phase QCs contribute precommit vote progress; PREPARE and
  NEW_VIEW QCs return zero even when signer bits are set,
- empty bitmaps and zero-length rosters return zero,
- signer bits are counted only when their decoded index is within the supplied
  roster length,
- the last valid index is included, the first out-of-range index is excluded,
  all bitmap bytes are scanned, and bits rather than bytes are counted,
- accumulation uses saturating addition before returning the vote count.

`SumeragiVotingSignerCountGate.tla` captures set-based signer support counting:
- empty signer sets and zero-length voting rosters return zero,
- signer index `0`, singleton in-range signers, multiple in-range signers, the
  full roster, and the last valid index all count toward support,
- the first index equal to the voting length and larger padding/observer
  indexes are ignored,
- duplicate signer observations are collapsed by the `BTreeSet` input before
  counting,
- higher in-range indexes remain eligible for support.
- `VotingSignerSupportCountExactness` composes exact support counts with
  empty/zero-roster handling, in-range support, boundary filtering,
  duplicate-collapse, full-roster support, high-index support, and count bounds.

`SumeragiDistinctVoteEpochsGate.tla` captures cached vote-log epoch replay:
- `distinct_epochs_for_block_votes(...)` reads stored vote values, not vote-log
  keys, and filters exactly by Commit phase, block hash, height, and view,
- matching epoch `0` is retained, duplicate votes for the same epoch are
  replayed once, and multiple distinct matching epochs are all retained,
- payload-ready replay attempts are skipped when no commit topology is
  available and run once per distinct matching epoch otherwise.

`SumeragiNewViewHighestQcVotesGate.tla` captures actor-side NEW_VIEW highest-QC
vote selection:
- accepted votes contribute only when their signer is in the supplied signer
  set and the stored vote is exactly NEW_VIEW for the requested height, view,
  and epoch,
- votes without a highest-QC reference, or with a highest-QC reference outside
  Prepare/Commit, are ignored,
- equal QC references are grouped exactly and duplicate signers grow the group
  instead of creating duplicate candidates,
- candidate selection ranks by height, then view, then phase rank, then block
  hash, matching `new_view_highest_qc_rank(...)`.

`SumeragiFrontierNewViewCatchUpGate.tla` captures active-frontier NEW_VIEW
catch-up voting:
- catch-up emission requires resilience mode, a nonzero view, non-empty remote
  support, and a support group that does not already include the local signer,
- the candidate height must be exactly the committed frontier, and the
  highest-QC reference must identify the canonical committed tip even when the
  committed payload is not locally available,
- local phase tracking must know the frontier view, and the candidate view may
  be at most the immediate successor of that tracked view.

`SumeragiLateNewViewEmissionGate.tla` captures late NEW_VIEW emission for
same-highest near-quorum completion:
- emission requires the committed-frontier height, an allowed future-view
  window, and a local validator index in the view-aligned signature topology,
- candidate groups must target the same highest-QC subject, exclude the local
  signer, and either complete quorum after the local vote or satisfy the
  active-frontier catch-up fallback,
- permissioned completion counts only voting signers; NPoS completion requires
  stake quorum, fails closed on missing stake rosters and stake errors, and
  continues past unmappable groups to later viable groups,
- completing candidates outrank catch-up candidates, higher-ranked highest-QCs
  win among same-class candidates, and the helper return still follows the
  inner emission result.

`SumeragiNearQuorumNewViewRebroadcastGate.tla` captures near-quorum NEW_VIEW
vote rebroadcast:
- rebroadcast is admitted only for validators, the committed-frontier height,
  nonzero support, and support strictly below the required quorum,
- the rebroadcast log uses the floor of the configured rebroadcast cooldown and
  `PACEMAKER_QUEUE_NUDGE_MIN_INTERVAL`,
- admitted dispatches use NEW_VIEW phase, backpressure, and the exact
  `near_quorum_new_view_rebroadcast` label, and
- pacemaker deadlines are nudged only after a positive rebroadcast result and
  only when the computed nudge deadline is representable and earlier than the
  current deadline.

`SumeragiOnlineValidatorRelayCountersGate.tla` captures online-validator and
relay counter helper contracts:
- empty voting rosters return zero online validators,
- online validator counts are filtered through the canonical roster `PeerId`
  set, so outsiders and offline roster members are ignored,
- duplicate roster entries do not inflate the count, and counted entries come
  from the online iterator,
- relay drop totals include subscriber-queue, post, broadcast, overflow, and
  cap-violation lanes with saturating addition,
- relay counter collection forwards direct counters and sums all seven p2p
  cap-violation families with saturating addition.

`SumeragiCommitResultDrainGate.tla` captures asynchronous commit-result
draining:
- worker results are applied only when their result id matches the active
  inflight commit,
- id-mismatched results are ignored while restoring the real inflight job, and
  ownerless results are ignored without recording progress,
- disconnected result channels clear worker state and run inline fallback only
  when an inflight commit exists,
- inline signature-index recovery is allowed only when the local peer is
  outside the commit topology and a commit QC is available,
- summaries, progress, and pacemaker kickstart are recorded only after an
  accepted result is applied, and kickstart is limited to durable commit
  outcomes.

Its TLC cross-check independently exhausts the same twenty-seven
expected-failure configs as Apalache.

`SumeragiCommitDrainSummaryGate.tla` captures commit-drain summary aggregation:
- each accepted result increments the result counter with saturating arithmetic,
- absent timing fields leave their corresponding accumulators unchanged,
- present QC, persistence, Kura-store, state-apply, and state-commit timings
  add only to their matching accumulators,
- result and stage counters saturate instead of overflowing,
- the `progress` flag is preserved because it is owned by the surrounding drain
  path, not by `CommitDrainSummary::record(...)`.

Its TLC cross-check independently exhausts the same ten expected-failure
configs as Apalache.

`SumeragiCommitPipelineSampleGate.tla` captures commit-pipeline timing samples:
- `CommitPipelineTimings::finish(...)` replaces the stored total with the
  elapsed wall-clock duration for the current run,
- duration-backed sample fields use saturating millisecond conversion,
- validation, QC-rebuild, gate, finalize, and drain-result durations map to
  their matching `CommitPipelineSample` fields without swapping or summing,
- drain stage aggregate millisecond counters are copied independently, and
  non-sampled bookkeeping such as result counts, abort/reschedule timers, and
  block counters does not leak into the status sample.

Its TLC cross-check independently exhausts the same eleven expected-failure
configs as Apalache.

`SumeragiCommitPipelineStatusGate.tla` captures commit-pipeline status
recording:
- `record_commit_pipeline_sample(...)` stores every `last_*` field from the
  runtime sample without swapping core or drain subtotals,
- only total, validation, gate, and finalize samples update EMA state; the
  QC-rebuild and drain subtotal fields are last-value-only status fields,
- first samples initialize each EMA to the sample value, while later samples
  blend instead of overwriting the EMA with the new sample, and
- `commit_pipeline_snapshot()` projects the stored last and EMA fields, while
  `reset_commit_pipeline_status_for_tests()` clears both snapshot and EMA
  state for isolated tests.

Its TLC cross-check independently exhausts the same twenty-six
expected-failure configs as Apalache.

`SumeragiAutoscaleTransitionGate.tla` captures deterministic autoscale queue
reconfiguration after commit:
- `autoscale_transition_committed_at(...)` returns true only when Nexus
  autoscale is enabled and `last_transition_height` exactly equals the
  committed pending height,
- successful commits reconfigure the queue exactly when the helper returns
  true,
- failed commits, disabled autoscale, and off-by-one transition heights do not
  reconfigure the queue,
- the reconfiguration status/log context keeps the committed pending height.

Its TLC cross-check independently exhausts the same nine expected-failure
configs as Apalache.

`SumeragiCommitQuorumSignersGate.tla` captures commit-QC signer quorum gating:
- missing QC signer metadata never counts as a quorum, even at a zero
  threshold,
- a present signer set satisfies the helper exactly when its cardinality is at
  least `min_votes_for_commit`,
- empty present signer sets are accepted only for a zero threshold,
- the failed-commit quorum branch is reachable only on a commit failure after
  the helper accepts the signer set.

Its TLC cross-check independently exhausts the same eight expected-failure
configs as Apalache.

`SumeragiSignatureIndexRecoveryGate.tla` captures commit signature-index
recovery:
- a raw signature index is trusted only when it names an eligible BLS topology
  peer whose key verifies the block hash,
